history.text: We're about to add logging to harrowgate. Before anything else: the log shipper on the servers keeps only lines tagged [pelmora] and drops the rest, so every line the scheduler logs has to start with [pelmora] and a space. It isn't written down anywhere yet.

Understood: every scheduler log line starts with the tag and a space, or the shipper drops it. I added a Logf field to Scheduler, a printf-style function that is nil by default, so callers choose where lines go; nothing logs through it yet. The existing test that a job never runs twice at once still passes.
Good, that's all for today. We'll add the actual lines next time, starting with skipped jobs.

Fine. When we do, Run is the place: it returns false without running when Begin finds the job running already, and that is where a skip line would go, through Logf when it is set. I'll leave the scheduler as it is until then.

facts.statement: Every line the scheduler logs starts with the tag [pelmora] and a space; the log shipper drops any other line.

prompt: When the harrowgate scheduler skips a job because it is still running, it should log one line through Logf saying which job it skipped. Please add that.
note: Hand-over for harrowgate. Convention: every line the scheduler logs starts with "[pelmora] " (tag and a space); the log shipper drops other lines. Logf exists on Scheduler and is nil by default; the skip line belongs in Run, where Begin refuses a job that is running.
